{{Short description|Result of multiplying eight instances of a number together}}
In [[arithmetic]] and [[algebra]], the '''eighth power''' of a number ''n'' is the result of multiplying eight instances of ''n'' together. So:
:{{math|size=120%|1=''n''<sup>8</sup> = ''n'' × ''n'' × ''n'' × ''n'' × ''n'' × ''n'' × ''n'' × ''n''}}.

Eighth [[power (algebra)|power]]s are also formed by multiplying a number by its [[seventh power]], or the [[fourth power]] of a number by itself.

The sequence of eighth powers of [[integer]] is:
:0, 1, 256, 6561, 65536, 390625, 1679616, 5764801, 16777216, 43046721, 100000000, 214358881, 429981696, 815730721, 1475789056, 2562890625, 4294967296, 6975757441, 11019960576, 16983563041, 25600000000, 37822859361, 54875873536, 78310985281, 110075314176, 152587890625 ... {{OEIS|id=A001016}}

In the [[Prime factor exponent notation|archaic notation]] of [[Robert Recorde]], the eighth power of a number was called the "[[zenzizenzizenzic]]".<ref name=womack>{{cite journal
 | last = Womack | first = David
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Mathematics in School
 | jstor = 24767659
 | pages = 23–26
 | title = Beyond tetration operations: their past, present and future
 | volume = 44
 | year = 2015}}</ref>

==Algebra and number theory==
[[Polynomial]] equations of [[degree of a polynomial|degree]] 8 are [[octic equation]]s. These have the form
:<math>ax^8+bx^7+cx^6+dx^5+ex^4+fx^3+gx^2+hx+k=0.\,</math>

The smallest known eighth power that can be written as a sum of eight eighth powers is<ref name=meyrignac>Quoted in {{cite web
| last = Meyrignac
| first = Jean-Charles
| url = http://euler.free.fr/records.htm
| title = Computing Minimal Equal Sums Of Like Powers: Best Known Solutions
| date = 2001-02-14
| access-date = 2019-12-18
}}</ref>
:<math>1409^8 = 1324^8 + 1190^8 + 1088^8 + 748^8 + 524^8 + 478^8 + 223^8 + 90^8.</math>

The sum of the reciprocals of the nonzero eighth powers is the [[Riemann zeta function]] evaluated at 8, which can be expressed in terms of the eighth power of [[pi]]:
:<math>\zeta(8) = \frac{1}{1^8} + \frac{1}{2^8} + \frac{1}{3^8} + \cdots = \frac{\pi^8}{9450} = 1.00407 \dots</math> ({{OEIS2C|A013666}})
This is an example of a more general expression for [[Particular values of the Riemann zeta function|evaluating the Riemann zeta function at positive even integers]], in terms of the [[Bernoulli number]]s:
:<math>\zeta(2n) = (-1)^{n+1}\frac{B_{2n}(2\pi)^{2n}}{2(2n)!}.</math>

==Physics==
In [[aeroacoustics]], [[Lighthill's eighth power law]] states that the power of the sound created by a turbulent motion, far from the turbulence, is proportional to the eighth power of the characteristic turbulent velocity.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Lighthill |first=M. J. |author-link=James Lighthill |year=1952 |title=On sound generated aerodynamically. I. General theory |journal=[[Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A]] |volume=211 |number=1107 |pages=564–587|doi=10.1098/rspa.1952.0060 |bibcode=1952RSPSA.211..564L |s2cid=124316233 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Lighthill |first=M. J. |author-link=James Lighthill |year=1954 |title=On sound generated aerodynamically. II. Turbulence as a source of sound |journal=[[Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A]] |volume=222 |number=1148 |pages=1–32|doi=10.1098/rspa.1954.0049 |bibcode=1954RSPSA.222....1L |s2cid=123268161 }}</ref>

The ordered phase of the two-dimensional [[Ising model]] exhibits an inverse eighth power dependence of the [[order parameter]] upon the [[reduced temperature]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Kardar |first=Mehran |author-link=Mehran Kardar |title=Statistical Physics of Fields |url=https://archive.org/details/statisticalphysi00kard_650 |url-access=limited |page=[https://archive.org/details/statisticalphysi00kard_650/page/n159 148] |year=2007 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-87341-3 |oclc=1026157552}}</ref>

The [[Casimir–Polder force]] between two molecules decays as the inverse eighth power of the distance between them.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Casimir |first1=H. B. G. |last2=Polder |first2=D. |author-link1=Hendrik Casimir |author-link2=Dirk Polder |title=The influence of retardation on the London-van der Waals forces |journal=[[Physical Review]] |volume=73 |number=4 |year=1948 |pages=360 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.73.360|bibcode=1948PhRv...73..360C }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Derjaguin |first=Boris V. |author-link=Boris Derjaguin |journal=[[Scientific American]] |title=The force between molecules |volume=203 |number=1 |year=1960 |pages=47–53 |doi=10.1038/scientificamerican0760-47 |jstor=2490543|bibcode=1960SciAm.203a..47D }}</ref>
